clue.text: Lad on vehicle shows bottle

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it, so the lad comes after the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy riding on a vehicle is displaying a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A carboy is a large rounded bottle, usually in a protective frame, for holding acids or other liquids.

clue.text: Net disagreement left out of superpower- PACE er rivalry?

annotationWithheld.why: Net disagreement left out of superpower- PACE er rivalry?: the held text has debris '- PACE er' inside 'superpower rivalry' (COLD WAR less L gives COD WAR), more than an OCR letter or two, and the scan crop is blank
annotationWithheld.clue: Net disagreement left out of superpower- PACE er rivalry?

clue.text: Arbitrator stopped early and fixed votes

indicators.note: the word for the arbitrator is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: a referee arbitrates in a game

indicators.note: fixed in the sense of rigged or rearranged, so the letters of 'and' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A referee halted a match early and a vote was rigged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopped early' trims REFEREE to REFERE; 'fixed' turns AND into NDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Referenda are public votes put to the whole electorate on a single question; the Latin plural of referendum.

clue.text: Compound source of meat and fish

parts.note: an ox provides beef
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A recipe's ingredients come from beef and fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxide is a chemical compound of oxygen with another element.

clue.text: Smarter young lady wears scarf in alternate places

annotationWithheld.why: Smarter young lady wears scarf in alternate places: LASS accounts for four letters but no reading of 'scarf in alternate places' gives C, IER around it; the clue as held may be garbled and no search found it
annotationWithheld.clue: Smarter young lady wears scarf in alternate places

clue.text: Devastatingly radiant and stately Mormon

indicators.note: something devastated is wrecked, so the letters of the two words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Mormon is described as stunningly radiant and dignified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Devastatingly' rearranges RADIANT and STATELY together; 'and' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Latter-day Saint is the name members of the Mormon church use for themselves.

clue.text: Top players begin to get pots?

parts.note: to begin is to start
urns are vessels or pots

explanation.surface: Stars of the show start by collecting trophies.
explanation.definitionFit: Star turns are the leading acts or performers on a bill.

clue.text: This is relative, as counsel will advise

explanation.surface: A relative acting the way a lawyer recommends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This is' only joins the clue to the first definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A relative by marriage is one sense; the other is the phrase read literally: what is within the law, which a barrister would advise.

clue.text: Set aside without emotion

explanation.surface: Putting something to one side coolly.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserved means booked or kept back, and also restrained and undemonstrative in manner.

clue.text: Flat, as vengeful Figaro was?

explanation.surface: Mozart's Figaro was gunning for his employer.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Marriage of Figaro, Figaro plots against Count Almaviva, so he is 'out for' the Count; boxing gives the other sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer knocked flat and not rising before ten is counted is out for the count; the opera plot gives the second sense.

clue.text: Hard duke's reportedly dubious following

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke

indicators.note: signals that the words are taken by how they sound when said

parts.note: iffy means dubious and a cult is a following

explanation.surface: A tough nobleman is said to have a questionable band of followers.
explanation.walkthrough: D plus IFFY CULT, spoken, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Difficult and hard are synonyms for something not easy to do.

clue.text: Originally, Ancient Mariner rejected maps

definitions.note: the definition is plural; the answer is a book of them

indicators.note: the starting letter of the word Ancient is taken
turned back, so the word for the mariner is written backwards

parts.note: a salt is an old sailor

explanation.surface: Coleridge's Ancient Mariner throws away his charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' is the reversal signal; 'salt' for an old sailor is a crossword convention, and the Coleridge surface hides it.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound collection of maps.

clue.text: Express runs beside road

indicators.note: the runs letter is placed next to the road, after it

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's main north-south road, written AI in crosswords
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A fast train runs alongside a road.
explanation.definitionFit: To air a view is to express it publicly.

clue.text: What's seen in a tour of Paris?

definitions.text: What's seen in a tour of Paris?

parts.words: What's seen in a tour of Paris?
parts.note: reads as a sightseeing question, but 'tour' is also the French word for tower, so 'a tour of Paris' is the city's famous tower

explanation.surface: Asking what sights a visitor to Paris takes in.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eiffel Tower is the best-known sight in Paris, called la tour Eiffel in French.

clue.text: One aiming for second child half heartedly

indicators.note: the heart of the word for child is its doubled middle letter; half of that pair is dropped

parts.note: a nipper is a small child

explanation.surface: Someone half-heartedly aiming to have a second baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half heartedly' removes one of the two Ps in NIPPER, leaving NIPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniper is a marksman who aims from a hidden position.

clue.text: Big strides, of course?

parts.note: strides is slang for trousers, and 'of course' means belonging to the golf course: baggy golfing knickerbockers

explanation.surface: Seems to be about taking long steps, naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Plus fours are loose breeches once standard golfing wear, hanging four inches below the knee.

clue.text: Good to keep doctor touring university round island

indicators.note: the doctor travels round the university, enclosing it
turned round, so the island's name is written backwards

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: A doctor on a university tour goes round an island, keeping well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is the reversal signal for the island, Napoleon's place of exile; 'Good to keep' reads as the start of the wordplay but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something durable lasts well, so it is good for keeping a long time.

clue.text: Café in Exeter emptied in club

indicators.note: the outer letters of Exeter go inside the club

parts.note: a brassie is an old name for a golf club, the number two wood

indicators.note: with all its inner letters removed, only the outer pair of the word remains

explanation.surface: A café in Exeter clears out its customers into a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emptied' keeps only the first and last letters of the city; a brassie is an old golf wood, a club the surface passes off as a nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal restaurant or café serving simple food and drink.

clue.text: Have nothing against working capital

indicators.note: set working, the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: O is the round figure for nothing

explanation.surface: Not objecting to working in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges O with AGAINST; 'Have' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Santiago is the capital city of Chile.

clue.text: If necessary, answer cheers press

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers
to press is to push

explanation.surface: Answering a toast when the press demands it.
explanation.definitionFit: At a push is an idiom meaning if really necessary or with some difficulty.

clue.text: No woman's contrary, I'd always agree

parts.note: the contrary of no is yes; 'contrary' governs both words
the opposite of woman is man

explanation.surface: Someone protesting that a contrary woman will always be agreed with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrary' is applied to both No and woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A yes-man always agrees with his superiors, so the definition is his own words.

clue.text: Colourless sort of china covering

parts.note: china is Cockney rhyming slang (china plate) for mate, and a pal is a kind of mate
a lid is a covering

explanation.surface: Plain white crockery with a lid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'china' looks like porcelain; in rhyming slang china plate = mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Pallid and colourless both describe a pale, wan face.

clue.text: Illegally trades stuff inside blocks on wheels?

indicators.note: the word for stuff goes inside the word for illegal trading

parts.note: to traffic is to deal illegally, as in drugs
to jam is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: Smuggled goods are crammed inside wheeled toy blocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' is the container signal; 'blocks on wheels' reads as toy bricks, but the blocks are blockages of cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic jams are blockages of vehicles on the road, playfully called blocks on wheels.

clue.text: Little animals hiding under a hood

indicators.note: in a down clue, the animals sit below the letter, coming after it

parts.note: mice are small animals

explanation.surface: Small creatures hide beneath a hood.
explanation.definitionFit: An amice is a liturgical vestment, a cloth or hood worn about the head and shoulders.

clue.text: Quiet tot carried round hospital, beginning to teethe

indicators.note: the sum encloses the other letters

parts.note: to tot up is to add, and a tot is a sum

indicators.note: the first letter of teethe is taken

explanation.surface: A silent toddler is taken round the hospital as it starts teething.
explanation.walkthrough: SUM goes round H and T; 'tot' looks like a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Shtum is Yiddish-derived slang for silent, as in keeping quiet.

clue.text: Bath salts prevent aches up front

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of the three words is taken

explanation.surface: Bath salts are recommended to stop aches.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is a city famous for its spa waters.
explanation.definitionFit: Bath is a well-known spa town in England, and a spa is a place for bathing.

clue.text: Peter's wearing gold for so long

indicators.note: the gold goes round the dying word, as clothes go round a wearer

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to peter out is to die away; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Saint Peter, dressed in gold, bids a long farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter' looks like a name but is the verb to peter (out).
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu and so long are both ways of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Distorted lunarnaut's broadcast

indicators.note: scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A moon traveller's transmission comes through garbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Unnatural can mean distorted or abnormal, departing from the natural form.

clue.text: Drunken sot straddling lines causes grief

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit on either side of the lines
the letters are reeling, so the word sot is rearranged

parts.note: verse is lines of poetry

explanation.surface: A drunk staggering across the road markings brings sorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' turns SOT into OTS, which straddles VERSE: O-VERSE-TS.
explanation.definitionFit: To overset is an old word for upset or overturn, so it means distress someone.

clue.text: Denim ruined -—- penny found inside loom

indicators.note: the penny letter is placed within the rearranged letters
spoilt, so the letters of denim are reworked

explanation.surface: A coin is discovered in ruined denim from a weaving loom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' turns DENIM into IMEND, with P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To loom is to appear threateningly close, as to impend does.
